commits.author: Haozhe Xie
commits.message:
build: replace maven-git-versioning-extension with a revision property

The extension calls maven-shared-utils, which Maven 3.10 no longer ships,
so every build on Maven 3.10 failed with NoClassDefFoundError. Use Maven's
CI-friendly ${revision} instead (default 0.0.0-SNAPSHOT) and derive the
release version with scripts/version.sh (same scheme: 1.0.1 on a tag,
1.0.2-SNAPSHOT after it). The Docker workflow and build scripts pass it
as -Drevision / the VOJ_VERSION build argument, so published images now
carry the real version, and the Dockerfiles move to Maven 3.10.0.

The Dockerfiles download Maven and ActiveMQ from dlcdn.apache.org, which
only keeps the latest release of each line, so a pinned version starts to
404 as soon as a newer one ships. Fall back to archive.apache.org, which
keeps every release, so the pinned versions keep building.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Haozhe Xie

feat(web): give every display language its own indexable URL

The display language lived only in the session, so one URL served
different languages. Pages now declare a canonical URL and hreflang
alternates built from the ?language= parameter. Problems, discussion
threads and contests are authored in a single language, so their
language versions share one canonical URL with no alternates and search
engines detect the language from the content. Also emit a valid BCP 47
<html lang> (zh-CN instead of zh_CN) and test the sitemap's public
problem query.

commits.author: Haozhe Xie
commits.message:
feat(docker): add Compose stack, persistent volume and reverse-proxy examples

Ship a self-host path alongside scripts/run-docker.sh (the no-compose
equivalent), so users can pick either entry point for the same two-container
stack:

- docker-compose.yml: bundled web + judger; the web is reachable to the judger
  via a `voj.web` network alias so the image's defaults resolve with no extra
  config. .env.example documents the overridable VOJ_* values.
- Persist the database in a named volume mounted at the image's MariaDB data
  directory (/var/lib/mariadb on the Ubuntu base), in both compose and
  run-docker.sh, so updating the image no longer wipes problems, users,
  submissions or problem test data (all of which live in MariaDB).
- docker/reverse-proxy/{nginx.conf,Caddyfile}: TLS in front, with the SSE
  judge-result stream un-buffered and given a long read timeout.
- Document all three in docker/README.md and the top-level README; gitignore .env.

Verified by building the web image from this branch and smoke-testing it: it
boots, the runtime VOJ_BASE_URL flows into the rendered asset URLs, and a marker
row survives a container destroy+recreate on the volume.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Haozhe Xie
commits.message:
feat: configure deployment from runtime environment variables

Move every deployment knob (database, mail, message queue, URLs, judger
token, context path) out of build-time baking and into ${VOJ_*}
placeholders resolved at runtime, so the images are generic and
reconfigurable with `docker run -e ...` -- no rebuild to change a secret
or to move behind a reverse proxy.

- web/judger voj.properties + web application.properties: deployment
  knobs become ${VOJ_*:default} placeholders
- PersistenceConfig: resolve the propertyConfigurer Properties bean
  through the Environment so template-facing values (url.cdn) no longer
  leak the literal ${...} placeholder
- web/judger Dockerfiles: drop the sed-baking and config build-args, set
  VOJ_* ENV defaults (the bundled demo MariaDB keeps a fixed `voj`
  password; a non-secret default token lets the two images interoperate)
- supervisord: read VOJ_JMS_BROKER_EMBEDDED (same var the app reads)
- run-docker.sh: pass secrets via -e at runtime, so VOJ_PULL images are
  configurable too; build-docker.sh keeps only the bundled-DB password arg
- run-web.sh: auto-host an embedded broker when none is reachable
- run-web/run-judger .sh and .bat: read connection settings from the
  VOJ_* env (the .bat scripts gain the same interface and broker fallback)
- docker docs: document the runtime configuration model

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Haozhe Xie
commits.message:
fix(web): tighten authorization on discussion mutations

Discussion mutations (create/edit/delete a thread or reply, vote, report)
were permitAll, so an anonymous POST reached the service and tripped a
NullPointerException on the user-group check instead of being denied
cleanly. Require authentication for POST /discussion/** at the security
layer, and add a null-safe canModify() backstop in DiscussionService so
the owner/administrator check never dereferences a null editor. Also fold
the authorization result into editDiscussionThread's isSuccessful flag,
which previously reported success (and logged an edit) to unauthorized
users even though nothing was persisted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Haozhe Xie
commits.message:
fix(web): restrict submission source code to its owner and administrators

A submission's source was readable by anyone. The detail page gated the
code behind a publicSubmissions option that defaulted to enabled, so it
served the source to every visitor (including anonymous ones), and the
submission-list JSON actions serialised the code column verbatim without
any check at all.

Make the source strictly private: canViewSourceCode now grants access
only to the submission's owner and to administrators, dropping the
publicSubmissions escape hatch entirely. Apply the same rule to the
list endpoints so getSubmissions / getLatestSubmissions strip the code
(and any source-echoing compiler-error log) for everyone else.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Haozhe Xie
commits.message:
fix(judger): report memory usage from MemAvailable, not MemFree

The heartbeat computed usage as (total - free) using the JVM bean's free
memory, which on Linux maps to /proc/meminfo's MemFree and counts
reclaimable buff/cache as "used". A healthy node thus reported ~96%
usage. Derive usage from MemAvailable in /proc/meminfo instead, matching
what `free` shows; fall back to the JVM bean on platforms without
/proc/meminfo.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Haozhe Xie
commits.message:
fix(judger): give compilation generous, configurable time/memory limits

The compile step was hardcoded to a 5s CPU limit with no memory cap, so
heavyweight toolchains were killed by the sandbox and reported as spurious
"Compile Error": Go's build driver and the JVM-based Kotlin compiler both
exceed 5s CPU (e.g. "compile: signal: killed").

Make the compile time limit configurable (default 20s) and add a compile
memory limit (default 512MB) so a "compiler bomb" cannot OOM the host while
still leaving room for kotlinc/the Go linker. Also add an --fsize disk-bomb
guard to the isolate runner, mirroring the native runner's RLIMIT_FSIZE.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Haozhe Xie
commits.message:
fix(web): reset submission to pending when rejudging

The rejudge action only enqueued a new judge task, leaving the record at
its old verdict. As a result the detail pages never re-rendered the
Pending-gated live judging stream, so a rejudge looked like a no-op, and
the expired-task guard (which only touches pending rows) could not mark
the task unjudgeable when no judger claimed it.

Clear the verdict, judge log, resource usage, score, executing judger and
execute time before sending the task, via a new resetSubmissionToPending
mapper call on the single-argument createSubmissionTask (the rejudge
path; fresh submissions are unaffected).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Haozhe Xie
commits.message:
build: derive Maven version from git tags

Adopt maven-git-versioning-extension so the project version is computed
from the current git ref at build time instead of a hand-maintained pom
value: a release tag yields the clean version (e.g. 1.0.0) and branch
builds yield the next-patch snapshot off the latest tag (e.g.
1.0.1-SNAPSHOT). The on-disk poms keep a 0.0.0-SNAPSHOT placeholder and
are never modified; product.version (shown in the UI) tracks it via
@project.version@. Releasing is now just creating a git tag.

commits.author: Haozhe Xie
commits.message:
fix(security): avoid ReDoS in Google Analytics code validation

The "<script.*>.*</script>" pattern had two unbounded .* quantifiers
separated only by a literal '>', which CodeQL flags as polynomial-time
backtracking (java/polynomial-redos, CWE-1333) on input like "<script"
followed by many '>'. Constrain the opening tag to "[^>]*>" so it stops
at the first '>', removing the ambiguity while preserving the rule that
the analytics snippet must be wrapped in a <script> tag.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Haozhe Xie
commits.message:
fix(security): avoid ReDoS in language command validation

isCompileCommandLegal / isRunCommandLegal matched ".*\{filename\}.*",
whose surrounding .* quantifiers let CodeQL flag polynomial-time
backtracking (java/polynomial-redos, CWE-1333) on crafted input. The
check only needs a substring test, so use String.contains("{filename}")
instead — same semantics, no regex, no backtracking.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
